elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, on thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor"; Section 2.1 was conformed to read "without termination rights other than as expressly provided in Section 9.4", removing the prior negation.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "on thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor" — 30 days, written, and no additional conditions or approvals attached.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees pro rata for the period after the effective date of termination" — express "pro rata" language, not merely a post-termination-period refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term." Retained Sections 9.1-9.3 are cause-based only (breach, insolvency, security/service/legal/IP failures), so no residual Vendor convenience right survives; Section 8.2 non-renewal is a natural-term RENEWAL matter, not mid-term T4C.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted right runs on thirty days' notice, which is shorter than the 60-90 day fallback window; this level is therefore incomplete (the preferred level is the operative target and is more favourable to Customer).

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee, penalty, instalment or contingent payment mechanic is imposed on Customer's convenience exit anywhere in the rendered text, so the cap is satisfied vacuously (nothing to cap).

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Vendor is given no convenience right at all ("Vendor has no right to terminate ... for convenience during a committed term"), which is at least as restrictive as an end-of-term-only right; remaining Vendor rights in 9.1-9.2 are cause-based.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Vendor has no convenience termination right during the committed term, so no Vendor convenience notice period is required.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: all four preferred elements appear in operative language — a Customer-only convenience right over the Agreement or any Order Form, 30 days' written notice, an express pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a committed term.

The finding status "deviation" is correct: the original document contained only cause-based termination rights (9.1 breach, 9.2 insolvency, 9.3 Vendor failures) in a three-year term, and Section 2.1 expressly negated termination rights, which is walk-away territory under this rule.

Minimality holds. The new clause is a concise insertion filling the vacant 9.4 slot and tracks the model language without extras (no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no added procedures or damages categories). The only other edit is the narrow conforming change to Section 2.1, which is necessary to remove a directly contradictory retained sentence; the Customer-adverse "without reduction rights" restriction was deliberately retained rather than deleted.

Intent preserved: Sections 8.1, 9.1-9.3 and 9.5 survive intact, the additive-remedies sentence in 9.5 is unaffected, and the take-or-pay commitment remains subject only to the new exit. Drafting repair to make before circulation (not an element failure): the inserted paragraph should carry the express number "9.4" so Section 2.1's cross-reference to "Section 9.4" has a labelled target rather than relying on its position between 9.3 and 9.5.

Fallback level is not complete solely because the notice period (30 days) sits outside the 60-90 day band; this is a more Customer-favourable outcome and no remediation is required since the preferred level is met.
